draft.title: Balanced equations
card: In a chemical reaction, atoms are rearranged, not created or destroyed. So the total mass of the products equals the total mass of the reactants.
A balanced equation shows this. It has the same number of each type of atom on both sides of the arrow.
To balance an equation, change the coefficients, the big numbers in front of formulas. Never change the small subscripts inside a formula, because that would make a different substance.
Example: 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O has 4 H atoms and 2 O atoms on each side. H₂ + O₂ → H₂O is not balanced, because the left has 2 O atoms and the right has 1.
draft.remember: Atoms are not lost or gained, so balance by changing coefficients only.

a.q: Why must a chemical equation be balanced?
opts: Atoms are not created or destroyed, so mass is conserved
Each reactant must have the same mass as each product
The number of molecules must be equal on both sides
Subscripts in formulas must match on both sides
a.why: Atoms are only rearranged in a reaction, so each type of atom must appear in the same number on both sides. The number of molecules can change, as in 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, so equal molecule counts are not required.
a.clue: Think about what happens to atoms during a reaction.

b.q: Mia balances H₂ + O₂ → H₂O by changing the product to H₂O₂. What is wrong with her method?
opts: Changing a subscript makes a different substance
Subscripts should be changed on the reactant side only
H₂O₂ has more atoms than the reactants
Only coefficients on the left side may be changed
b.why: H₂O₂ is hydrogen peroxide, not water, so Mia has changed the reaction instead of balancing it. Balancing uses coefficients, which change the amount of a substance but not what it is.
b.clue: Water and hydrogen peroxide are different substances.

a.best: Atoms are not created or destroyed, so mass is conserved

b.best: Changing a subscript makes a different substance
